source.author: verg
source.text: Limen erat caecaeque fores et pervius usus tectorum inter se Priami, postesque relicti a tergo, infelix qua se, dum regna manebant, saepius Andromache ferre incomitata solebat ad soceros, et avo puerum Astyanacta trahebat.
source.text_original: Limen erat caecaeque fores et pervius usus / tectorum inter se Priami, postesque relicti / a tergo, infelix qua se, dum regna manebant, / saepius Andromache ferre incomitata solebat / ad soceros, et avo puerum Astyanacta trahebat.
source.text_english: There was a threshold and blind doors, and a passage through the roofs linking Priam’s chambers with one another, and the doorposts left behind at the rear, unhappy place where, while the kingdom still stood, Andromache had been accustomed more often to go unescorted to her in-laws, and to lead little Astyanax to his grandfather.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nec Peleus fretus soceris et coniuge diva defuit, ac prora splendet tua cuspis ab alta, Aeacide: tantum haec aliis excelsior hastis, quantum Peliacas in vertice vicerat ornos.
reuse.text_original: nec Peleus fretus soceris et coniuge diva / defuit, ac prora splendet tua cuspis ab alta, / Aeacide: tantum haec aliis excelsior hastis, / quantum Peliacas in vertice vicerat ornos.
reuse.text_english: Nor was Peleus lacking, relying on his father-in-law and his divine wife, and your spearpoint gleams from the lofty prow, Aeacides: only this spear is higher than the others by as much as it had surpassed the Pelian mountain-ashes on the summit.
